variables.input:
fetch logs, scanLimitGBytes: -1
| filter dt.system.bucket == "custom_sen_low_logs_lima_shared"
| filter contains(log.source, "hostBillingModel")
| filter contains(content, "host-billing-model:")
| parse content, "LD 'host-billing-model:' LD:logKind SPACE 'JSON:' JSON:query"
| fields timestamp, logKind, query
| fieldsFlatten query 
| fieldsRemove query
| dedup query.tenantUuid
| fieldsKeep query.tenantUuid
| limit 10000

0.title: Monitored hosts and the potential host capping effect
0.query:
fetch logs, scanLimitGBytes: -1

// filter for existing hosts
| filter dt.system.bucket == "custom_sen_low_logs_lima_shared"
| filter matchesPhrase(log.source, "hostBillingModel")
| filter matchesPhrase(content, "host-billing-model:")
| fieldsKeep content
| parse content, "LD 'host-billing-model:' LD:logKind SPACE 'JSON:' JSON:query"
| fieldsRemove content
| fieldsFlatten query
| filter logKind == "host"
| filter in(query.tenantUuid, $selectedTenants)
| dedup query.hostMeId

// matching different rules
| fieldsAdd matchesRuleIn = in(query.hostNames, splitString($ruleDefinition, ","))
| fieldsAdd matchesRuleStartsWith = startsWith(query.hostNames, $ruleDefinition)
| fieldsAdd matchesRuleEndsWith = endsWith(query.hostNames, $ruleDefinition)
| fieldsAdd matchesRuleContains = contains(query.hostNames, $ruleDefinition)

// helpers for coalescing the final match in the end
| fieldsAdd helperRuleIn = if($cappingRule == "IN", then: matchesRuleIn, else: null)
| fieldsAdd helperRuleStartsWith = if($cappingRule == "STARTS_WITH", then: matchesRuleStartsWith, else: null)
| fieldsAdd helperRuleEndsWith = if($cappingRule == "ENDS_WITH", then: matchesRuleEndsWith, else: null)
| fieldsAdd helperRuleContains = if($cappingRule == "CONTAINS", then: matchesRuleContains, else: null)

// does the selected rule match?
| fieldsAdd matchesAnyRule = coalesce(helperRuleIn, helperRuleStartsWith, helperRuleEndsWith, helperRuleContains)
| fieldsAdd status = if(
    matchesAnyRule,
    then: "🟢 Would be capped",
    else: "🔴 Would not be capped"
  )

| fieldsAdd bytesToGib = power(1024, 3)

// TODO: document that this does not perfectly reflect the whole billing logic (e.g. rounding/minimum memory)
| fieldsAdd cappingGib = toLong($cappingGib)
| fieldsAdd cappingBytes = cappingGib * bytesToGib
| fieldsAdd cappedHostBytes = arrayMin(array(cappingBytes, query.totalReportedHostMemoryBytes))
| fieldsAdd cappedHostBytes = if(
    matchesAnyRule,
    then: cappedHostBytes,
    else: query.totalReportedHostMemoryBytes
  )
| fieldsAdd hostBytesDifference = query.totalReportedHostMemoryBytes - cappedHostBytes

| fields
    query.hostMeId, alias: `Host ME-ID`,
    query.hostNames, alias: `Hostname`,
    splitString(query.ips, ","), alias: `Host IPs`,
    query.totalReportedHostMemoryBytes / bytesToGib, alias: `Real Memory`,
    cappedHostBytes / bytesToGib, alias: `Memory after capping`,
    hostBytesDifference / bytesToGib, alias: `Reduction by capping`, 
    status, alias: `Capping status`
| sort Hostname asc

1.content:
# Host Capping Evaluation Dashboard

This dashboard shows a list of all recently monitored and billed hosts of the selected tenants, together with crucial information for a potential host capping configuration, most importantly the hostname and ip-addresses reported by the hosts agent. Please note that this is the only information host capping rules can be based upon. Especially for hostnames, capping rules must be designed to match exactly the format as displayed here (including the case of letters).

**Note: Using this dashboard will not configure any host capping rules. It's purely read-only to test the potential effect of host capping rules.**

## Basic Instructions

* Always use a dashboard query timeframe of **at least** 24h to get accurate results.
* Use the control `selectedTenants` on the top of the dashboard to select 1 or multiple tenants. The dashboard will list all monitored and billed hosts connected to theses tenants (within the query time frame).
* Choose the type of capping rule you want to test via the `cappingRule` control on top of the dashboard.
* Enter the capping rule definition in the `ruleDefinition` control on top of the dashboard (see section below for further instructions).
* Enter the amount of GiB matching hosts should be capped to in the `cappingGib` control on top of the dashboard. This will be used to show information about the potential effect of the capping in the table.

## Displayed data

* **Host ME-ID**: The identifier of the host in the ME-Model.
* **Hostname**: The hostname as reported by the OneAgent to the billing logic. This is what the capping rules will evaluate on.
* **Host IPs**: The ip addresses as reported by the OneAgent to the billing logic. Even though this dashboard does not allow to, the product is able to base capping rules on these as well.
* **Real Memory**: The real memory of the host as reported by the OneAgent. This is the billed memory without any applied capping.
* **Memory after capping**: The billed memory of the host after evaluating the capping rule. Without a matching capping rule, this is the same as the real memory.
* **Reduction by capping**: Shows by how much the billed memory would be reduced by the capping rule. This is 0 if the capping rule does not match.
* **Capping status**: Shows wether the capping rule matches the host (🟢) or not (🔴).

## Capping Rule Descriptions

### IN

Using this rule, you can define a list of hostnames via a comma-separated list in the `ruleDefinition` control. All hosts matching **exactly** (case sensitive) one of the entered hostnames would be capped.

For example, given `hostA,hostB.example.com`, only the following hostnames would match:

* `hostA`
* `hostB.example.com`

The following hostnames would **not** match:

* `hosta`
* `hostA.example.com`
* `hostb.example.com`

### CONTAINS

Using this rule, you can define a phrase that needs to be contained within the hostname via the `ruleDefinition` control. All hosts containing the given phrase (case sensitive) would be capped.

For example, given `.department.`, the following hostnames would match:

* `test.department.example.com`
* `.department.example.com`
* `.department.`

The following hostnames would **not** match:

* `department.example.com`
* `test.department`
* `test.DEPARTMENT.example.com`

### STARTS_WITH

Using this rule, you can define a phrase that needs to be the prefix of a hostname via the `ruleDefinition` control. All hosts starting exactly with the given phrase (case sensitive) would be capped.

For example, given `database`, the following hostnames would match:

* `database.example.com`
* `database12.example.com`
* `database534`

The following hostnames would **not** match:

* `mydatabase.example.com`
* `www.database.example.com`


### ENDS_WITH

Similar to `STARTS_WITH` but the phrase must be a suffix.

## Remarks

This dashboard does only vaguely emulate the behavior of a configured host capping on a real tenant. Its main purpose is to provide the list of existing hosts and their names for the sake of defining (and testing) capping rules before they are put in a contract with the customer. The actual billing logic in the product is obviously more complex and we can't cover everything here. Examples of things not covered in this dashboard:

* Even if this dashboard allows to, in reality host capping can not go below the minimal billable memory of a host. For most hosts, the minimum memory used for billing is 4 GiB.
* Host capping does not apply to application-only monitored hosts, even if this dashboard would list them.
